themes_detail.label: Water Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints spiked to 15 THIS WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average (208% increase, z-score 4.1), while standing water complaints exploded to 4 last week vs. 0.1 baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72), signaling potential pipe breaks, flooding, or drainage failures across Lower Manhattan.
evidence: Water System complaints: 15 THIS WEEK vs. 4.9 weekly average (208% spike, z-score 4.1)
Standing Water complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (3100% spike, z-score 11.72 — highest severity spike in dataset)
Converges with long-standing CB budget request for street infrastructure repair
reporting_angles: Investigate whether NYC DEP has identified pipe breaks or flooding hotspots in Lower Manhattan; request internal reports from past 2 weeks
Doorknock affected residents in high-complaint areas to document property damage, basement flooding, or service disruptions

themes_detail.label: Commercial Construction Safety Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance/Facility complaints surged to 29 THIS WEEK vs. 6.5 weekly average (346% increase, z-score 5.86), while Door/Window complaints hit 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 baseline (540% spike, z-score 4.85), alongside Scaffold Safety complaints of 3 two weeks ago (1100% spike, z-score 4.16), suggesting active construction projects creating unsafe conditions.
evidence: Maintenance/Facility complaints: 29 THIS WEEK vs. 6.5 weekly average (346% spike, z-score 5.86)
Door/Window complaints: 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score 4.85)
Scaffold Safety complaints: 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 4.16)
1,268 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (1,091 alteration projects) — active construction density unusually high
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints against DOB permit database to pinpoint which active projects on Franklin Street and Cliff Street (ULURP applications filed) are generating safety violations
File FOIL for DOB violation notices issued to contractors in past 2 weeks; interview Department of Buildings about enforcement

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retail Expansion Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis Retailer complaints jumped to 4 last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% increase, z-score 4.91), indicating rapid expansion or operational issues at legal cannabis shops in Lower Manhattan.
evidence: Cannabis Retailer complaints: 4 last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 4.91)
No prior context of cannabis retail issues in district — suggests new shops opening or enforcement action
reporting_angles: Identify which licensed cannabis retailers opened in CD 101 in past 4 weeks; what are the specific complaints (odor, loitering, operating hours violations)?
Interview SLA and Office of Cannabis Management about enforcement activity and whether residential complaints are triggering inspections

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial Noise complaints nearly doubled to 48 last week vs. 19.4 weekly average (148% increase, z-score 4.87), concentrated among 283 total noise complaints over 90 days, suggesting hospitality, construction, or entertainment venue expansion.
evidence: Commercial Noise complaints: 48 last week vs. 19.4 weekly average (148% spike, z-score 4.87)
Noise represents 974 of 6,148 total complaints (15.8% of all 311 traffic) — persistent baseline issue
Converges with high DOB alteration permit volume (1,091 permits) — construction noise likely contributor
reporting_angles: Map which blocks/venues are generating repeat commercial noise complaints; cross-reference against recently approved liquor licenses or restaurant permits
Interview residents in high-complaint zones (likely SoHo, Tribeca, FiDi) about nightlife expansion and enforcement response

themes_detail.label: Street and Sidewalk Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk Condition complaints rose to 17 two weeks ago vs. 9.4 weekly average (81% increase, z-score 3.95), part of a broader 653 Street Condition complaints over 90 days, reflecting deferred maintenance across Lower Manhattan.
evidence: Sidewalk Condition complaints: 17 two weeks ago vs. 9.4 weekly average (81% spike, z-score 3.95)
Street Condition is 3rd-highest complaint category overall (653 complaints over 90 days)
Converges with long-standing CB budget requests for street light repair and street infrastructure upgrade
reporting_angles: Request DOT asset condition data for CD 101 sidewalks and street segments; identify maintenance backlog
Visual reporting: document specific hazardous sidewalk locations (trip hazards, potholes, tree damage) affecting foot traffic
